subject.title: fix(talk): reject malformed relay audio base64

question: Should Talk relay clients be required to send canonical standard or URL-safe Base64, with formerly permissive legacy encodings rejected at the gateway boundary?
rationale: The code deliberately changes externally supplied RPC input acceptance; tests and live proof establish the mechanics, but only the owner can confirm whether that compatibility break is intended for existing Talk clients.

options.title: Accept strict relay input
options.body: Merge with the current shared decoder and treat canonical standard/Base64url as the supported Talk relay audio contract.

options.title: Preserve broader legacy decoding
options.body: Revise the decoder to retain any previously supported non-canonical encodings if compatibility with those clients is required.

recommendation.title: Accept strict relay input
recommendation.body: Merge with the current shared decoder and treat canonical standard/Base64url as the supported Talk relay audio contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to the PR and authored the latest current-head boundary tests.
